served: MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast
results: 1. synkinesis assessment (eye closure with platysma/frontalis): co-contraction of eye closure with the left platysma and left frontalis; right lower-lip curling on speech and mastication
2. palpebral fissure width both sides: narrowed LEFT palpebral fissure from established synkinesis
3. family history: five of fourteen siblings have had a facial palsy; two affected brothers had recurrent episodes with synkinesis
4. MRI brain and internal auditory canal with contrast: no tumour, no perineural enhancement, no central lesion

5. clinical course: left facial palsy treated with acyclovir 400 mg five times daily for 10 days and prednisone 50 mg for five days with taper; right palsy at age 64 with retroauricular pain, hyperacusis and dysgeusia; right synkinesis appeared five months later
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Familial recurrent Bell's palsy (familial idiopathic facial nerve palsy) — hereditary predisposition to facial nerve inflammation, likely autosomal dominant with variable penetrance

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome (would need fissured tongue and orofacial edema to confirm)
2. Lyme disease (neuroborreliosis) — bilateral facial palsy is classic, though no tick exposure or erythema migrans reported and MRI normal
3. Neurosarcoidosis or other infiltrative granulomatous disease — though normal contrast MRI and absence of systemic features make this less likely
dx: Familial recurrent Bell's palsy (familial idiopathic facial nerve palsy) — hereditary predisposition to facial nerve inflammation, likely autosomal dominant with variable penetrance
